title: Sedation (medicine-induced sleep)
also: being put to sleep for a procedure
what: Medicine is given into a vein and you fall into a light sleep. The procedure goes calmly, and you usually do not remember it.
why: So a test or procedure can be done without fear or discomfort. For example, a gastroscopy or a colonoscopy.
duration: sedation lasts as long as the procedure, and waking up usually takes 30 to 60 minutes
tell_doctor: Heart or lung disease, or sleep apnea
If you have had problems with anesthesia before

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 hours. Clear water is fine until the time your clinic tells you.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Tell the doctor what you take. They will decide what to take in the morning.

prepare.title: Someone with you
prepare.text: You cannot drive after sedation. Arrange for someone to pick you up.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes. Take off jewelry and contact lenses.

steps: A small tube is put into a vein, and a sensor is clipped on your finger
A nurse or anesthetist gives you the medicine
Within a minute, you fall asleep
Your breathing and pulse are watched during the procedure
You wake up and rest in a recovery room until you feel yourself again
feel: Slight warmth or burning in the vein as the medicine goes in
after: Do not drive for the rest of the day
Do not sign important papers or make big decisions until the next day
You can eat and drink when the doctor says it is OK
It is best to have someone with you until the evening
red_flags: Trouble breathing or chest pain: call emergency services
Strong sleepiness that does not go away for several hours

faq.q: Is sedation the same as general anesthesia?
faq.a: Not quite. The sleep is light, and you breathe on your own. It is gentler than general anesthesia.

faq.q: Why can't I drive after sedation?
faq.a: The medicine slows your reactions for several more hours, even if you feel fine.

reminders.text: Procedure with sedation tomorrow. Arrange who will pick you up. Eat only until the time your clinic gave you.
